note: Predictions of PREREGISTRATION §8, evaluated after the run. Each is left exactly as written.

K2.evidence: SPDX licence list re-fetched at the end of the session: version 3.29.0 both times, corpus digest 73363f6622045c5a4cebc39af0bedf3bbe5cc5f212549a56aae249cdcf8315ec both times.

K3.evidence: All four independents: pure standard library (only `re`, and `__future__` in one), no forbidden import, no dynamic escape, a module-level score(), and 1,480 of 1,480 inputs returning the contract's shape with no exception. NOTE: the check itself had to be repaired twice before it measured what it said — see data/k3-run1-defective.json and data/k3-run2-defective.json.

P1.text: At least one pair among the delivered implementations disagrees on the family set of at least 10 of the 740 arm-C texts.
P1.evidence: Worst pair I-B vs I-C: 107 disagreements of 740. Best pair I-A vs R-ship: 29. All ten pairs exceed 10.

P2.text: R-def returns 'named' for the canonical MIT text, and at least 3 of 4 independents return 'placeholder' for it.
P2.evidence: R-def: named. I-A, I-B, I-C, I-D: placeholder, 4 of 4. The second hand catches the known defect unanimously.

P3.text: At least one independent reproduces defect 1 — returns 'named' for the canonical MIT text.
P3.evidence: 0 of 4. Every independent required a year-shaped token after the marker, which the boilerplate sentence has not. On THIS defect the failures were not correlated — but see the adjudication, where on four other inputs all four failed together.

P4.text: On at least one input a majority of delivered independents agree on a verdict differing from R-ship, and hand-adjudication finds the independents right — a defect still shipped in the 09-18 instrument.
P4.evidence: 6 of the 11 unanimous disagreements are one defect in R-ship: a copyright notice written 'Copyright (C) …' with a capital C is not recognised at all. It sits inside 09-18's own repair of defect 3. See data/adjudication.json.

P5.text: The number of arm-C texts on which the four independents disagree among themselves is greater than the number on which all four agree with each other but differ from R-ship.
P5.evidence: 127 against 11. The second hand is noisy before it is right: for every case where it convicts, it produces about eleven where it cannot agree with itself.

P6.text: Under the strict oracle, at least 95 % of R-ship's positive family identifications fall on member identifiers.
P6.evidence: R-ship 25.35 %, and every independent between 13.56 % and 27.48 %. The refutation is about the oracle, not the instruments, and the pre-registration said so before the run: 740 SPDX identifiers against a 24-name vocabulary, with the list carrying dozens of texts that genuinely carry another family's operative grant. What the oracle delivered was not a score but a LIST, and the adjudication came out of it.
